summary.text: A preterm female baby, birth weight 600 g and blood group B-positive developed hemolytic anemia with severe jaundice on the 1st day that did not respond to phototherapy (bilirubin 18 mg/dl, hemoglobin 13 g/dl).

Workup showed blood group B Rh (D) positive, Jk (a) positive, DAT 3+ positive for IgG, and anti-B in the acid eluate; the baby antibody screen and eluate screen were negative, and antibody identification and the maternal titers were not tested in the baby. ABO HDFN was concluded and HDFN due to anti-Jk (a) was ruled out.

A double-volume exchange transfusion with reconstituted whole blood plus phototherapy raised hemoglobin from 13 to 16 g/dl and lowered bilirubin from 18 to 13 mg/dl; the baby was stabilized in the NICU for 1 week and referred to a higher center for complications of prematurity and low birth weight.

summary.text: A 31-year-old HbE beta-thalassemia primigravida with PPROM, hypothyroidism, splenomegaly and portal venous hypertension was admitted with anemia (hemoglobin 4.7 g/dL preoperatively), received phenotype-matched PRBCs on the day of admission and the next day, and had an emergency cesarean section on day 2 at 24 weeks gestational age with one intraoperative PRBC unit (postoperative hemoglobin 10.3 g/dL); the transfusions were uneventful.

After delivery her antibody screen, previously negative, was positive; anti-Jk (a) was identified, DAT was 3+ positive with IgG specificity, the eluate contained anti-Jk (a), anti-B IgG titer was 4096 by tube and up to 16384 in CAT, and anti-Jk (a) titer was 8. Two of five typed PRBC units issued on the day of the cesarean were Jk (a) antigen positive.

Two weeks later she developed symptoms suggestive of DHTR with hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL and was given two units of Jk (a)-negative PRBCs with conservative management; hemoglobin rose to 9.8 g/dL without transfusion-related adverse events, and Jk (a)-negative PRBCs and vigilant follow-up were advised.
